display: Melbourne demolition contractor with a six-person crew in Brunswick. I recently recovered about 3 cubic metres of 1890s Baltic pine and Tasmanian blackwood from a Carlton terrace and want it to be used again.

signals.text: I've got about three cubes of 140-year-old Baltic pine and blackwood in my yard and I want it to go to someone who'll actually use it, not a skip or a mulch chipper.
I don't know any furniture makers, and my architect mate says that's who I should be talking to.
Salvage yards won't take it nailed and offer firewood prices, about $200 a cube de-nailed, so I'm looking for a better buyer or partner.
Tip fees are running about $3,100 a week and are hurting my margins. Any timber I can move on without dumping it helps.
The yard is small and the timber has to be out within about two months.
The boards are mostly decent lengths but full of nails and old bitumen glue, so I can only spare about half a day of crew time to prep them.
Facebook Marketplace gave me five messages, two asking if it was free and one wanting delivery to Geelong. I can't be doing lots of back-and-forth messaging.
I start a warehouse strip-out in Brunswick on 6 October with a hard 15 October finish, so I'm stretched for the next fortnight.
I've got a young crew member with potential who won't wear his dust mask unless I yell at him. I'd like better ways to get safety habits to stick with young tradies.
My back goes out some days and I can't lift. I'd like less of the heavy handling to fall on me.
Insurance is up 18 percent and loan repayments are tight, so I'm watching every cost that doesn't earn money.
I hate seeing good old timber wasted. My father was a carpenter and it would have upset him.
I've got a V8 engine rebuild stalled in the garage, waiting on a gasket set from Adelaide, and I haven't touched it in weeks.

offers.text: About 3 cubic metres of hand-planed 1890s Baltic pine floorboards and some Tasmanian blackwood skirting, mostly good lengths, stacked and covered. It needs de-nailing and cleaning.
Regular supply of reclaimed Victorian, Edwardian and 1930s timber from terrace and shed strip-outs. I'd flag the good stuff before it goes in a skip if someone wants a standing arrangement.
Licensed demolition and strip-out crew of six, with a white card, asbestos awareness and working-at-heights tickets, for renovators and small builders around Melbourne.
Two tip trucks, a bobcat, a mini excavator, scaffolding and a dust extraction rig. I can haul, load or clear a site.
Twenty-five years of knowledge of period houses: what's under the lino, what's behind the plaster, how Victorian, Edwardian and 1930s construction was built and where the good materials hide.
Can read a house before demolition and say what's worth salvaging, which helps architects and renovators plan reuse.
Contacts with a couple of Melbourne architects and a salvage yard in Thornbury.
Yard space in Brunswick for temporary storage of salvaged material. It's limited, but I can hold stock for a short pickup window.
Can coach junior netball and mentor a young person in the trades.
Can restore classic Australian cars and rebuild Holden 253 V8s, and I'm happy to swap know-how.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I'm a furniture maker in Melbourne and I'm looking for old-growth Baltic pine or Tasmanian blackwood. I don't mind pulling nails and I can collect it myself.
catchers.can: Ray has about 3 cubes of 1890s Baltic pine and blackwood ready to go. He can set a price and a pickup window within his two-month deadline.
catchers.confirm: Can you collect from Brunswick yourself within the next six to eight weeks, and are you fine with de-nailing boards that still have bitumen glue on them?

catchers.hypo: I'm renovating a Victorian terrace and I'd love to put original-style Baltic pine floorboards back in the front rooms. Do you know where to get genuine reclaimed boards?
catchers.can: Ray can supply the 1890s boards from his Carlton job or flag similar timber from future strip-outs. He can also advise on matching and laying period flooring.
catchers.confirm: Do you need genuine reclaimed boards from the period (not new timber made to look old), and can you take them in random lengths?

catchers.hypo: I run a small cafe or office fit-out and want reclaimed timber for a counter, shelves or feature wall. Can you supply reclaimed material and strip out what's already there?
catchers.can: Ray can combine the salvaged timber with strip-out labour and equipment, so one crew clears the old fit-out while the good boards are held back for reuse.
catchers.confirm: Is this a Melbourne-area job where you could accept rough, nailed salvaged boards in random lengths and treat them yourself?

catchers.hypo: I'm an architect or builder with a client who wants salvaged heritage materials kept on site or reused. Who can pull a period house apart carefully and hold the good timber?
catchers.can: Ray's crew can do a selective strip-out and set aside floorboards, skirting and joinery. His architect contacts, including Dave, can help with the design side.
catchers.confirm: Is the house pre-1940 and is reuse of materials a real requirement for the client, as opposed to nice-to-have?

catchers.hypo: I run a men's shed, school workshop or community woodworking group and we'd love donated hardwood to teach with. We can do the de-nailing ourselves.
catchers.can: Ray could donate or heavily discount some of the boards, particularly offcuts and shorter lengths, if the group collects them and does the de-nailing.
catchers.confirm: Does your group have the people and the tools to de-nail and prep boards, and can you collect from Brunswick in one trip?

catchers.hypo: I'm a set designer, prop maker or event builder and need weathered period timber that looks authentic. Where can I get large quantities cheaply?
catchers.can: Ray can sell nailed, imperfect boards by the cube as they are, which is exactly what many prop and set builders want.
catchers.confirm: Are you happy to take timber as-is, with nails and glue residue, and pick it up within about two months?

catchers.hypo: I'm a parent or coach at a local netball club and my son or daughter wants to get into a trade. Do you know anyone who'd take on a keen apprentice or labourer?
catchers.can: Ray runs a six-person demolition crew and coaches netball, so he can talk about trade pathways and may have room for a keen young worker.
catchers.confirm: Is the young person at least 17 or 18, willing to do physical site work, and open to wearing full safety gear?

catchers.hypo: I'm a small builder who needs a demolition crew at short notice for a strip-out. We need a licensed contractor who knows old buildings.
catchers.can: Ray's crew can take Melbourne strip-outs of terraces, sheds and warehouses with their own trucks, bobcat, excavator and dust extraction, once the 15 October warehouse job is done.
catchers.confirm: Is the site in the greater Melbourne area, and do you need the work after mid-October?

catchers.hypo: I have a Holden Kingswood or a 253 V8 that needs a rebuild. Do you know anyone who's done one and could share what to watch for?
catchers.can: Ray is partway through a 1972 Kingswood engine rebuild and can swap tips on parts sourcing and the 253 V8.
catchers.confirm: Is your car an older Holden with a 253 V8, rather than a different engine?

forbids.text: Won't spend more than about half a day of crew time de-nailing or prepping the timber.
Won't run online listings that need lots of back-and-forth messaging or free-giveaway haggling.
The timber has to leave the yard within about two months because there's no room to keep it longer.
Can't deliver long distances, for example to Geelong, as a favour. Collection from Brunswick is the default.
Won't sell the good boards at firewood prices.
Can't do heavy lifting myself on bad back days.
Won't work around the 6 to 15 October warehouse strip-out unless it is urgent.

projects.name: Second life for the Carlton timber
projects.text: Find a good home for about 3 cubic metres of 1890s Baltic pine and Tasmanian blackwood from a Carlton terrace. It needs de-nailing and cleaning, and has to be moved out of the yard within about two months.
roles_needed: reclaimed timber buyer or flooring restorer
person or group able to de-nail and prep boards
someone with a ute or truck for collection

policy.t1: When there's a real lead, I'll share the quantities, board lengths and condition, the nails and glue, the tip-fee pressure, the two-month deadline, and what price I'd consider.
policy.t2: Once trust is established and I know who I'm dealing with, I'll talk about my back problems and the business finances.
policy.never: Anything about family arguments or private household matters.
